DynamicCodeRegion.description:
A dynamic code region where code ran.

The emulator watches the memory that the guest allocates, for example with ``VirtualAlloc``, and
adds a region when the guest runs code in the region. With ``memory.dynamic_code_contents``, the
emulator adds one more snapshot to ``contents`` each time that code runs in the region after the

limit_reached.description: True if the region changed and code ran in it again after the last snapshot that ``memory.dynamic_code_contents.limit`` allows. Absent when ``memory.dynamic_code_contents`` is off.

count.description: Limit that ended the run: ``limits.api_calls`` of the config for ``api_call_limit``, ``limits.api_loop_calls`` for ``api_loop_limit``, or ``limits.instructions`` for ``instruction_limit``.

module.description: File name of the module, such as ``sample.exe`` or ``kernel32.dll``, the same as ``memory.modules[].name``. Only for a part of a module image.

section.description: Name of the section, such as ``.text``, or ``headers`` for the PE headers. Absent for a region that is not part of a module image, for a module image with no sections, and for an address in a module image that is outside the headers and the sections. In the last two cases, the region is the full image.

accesses.description: Read, write and execute counts of the regions and the symbols. Only with ``memory.accesses``.

dynamic_code.description: Dynamic code regions where code ran in the run, one entry for each region, in the order of the first time that code ran in the region.

coverage.description: Sorted addresses of the instructions that ran. Only with ``code.coverage``.
coverage.title: Coverage

dropped_files.description: Files that the guest wrote completely, up to the end of the run. User mode only.
dropped_files.title: Dropped Files

memory.description: Memory regions and modules at the end of the run. User mode only.

In an image, it reads only the strings that the guest changed after the load. These strings often are decoded data.

execs.description: Number of instructions that ran at the symbol address.

TracePosition.description: Position of an event: the instruction count, the thread, the process and the pc.

tick.description: Instruction count of the run at the time of the event, as in ``instruction_count`` of the run. The events of a run are in tick order. Absent when no option counts the instructions.
tick.title: Tick

tid.description: ID of the thread that did the operation.
tid.title: Tid

pid.description: ID of the process that did the operation.
pid.title: Pid

For an event that the code of an API makes, such as a file, registry, memory, process, thread or network event, also the address of the call: the same ``pc`` as the ``api`` event of the call. Such an event comes just before the ``api`` event of its call, with the same ``tick``.

description:
Report of one emulation: the input metadata, the runs and the payloads.

Machine words are ``0x``-prefixed hex strings: addresses, pointers,
handles, raw argument values, return values, register values and exception
codes. A 64-bit word can be above 2**53 or 2**63, and JavaScript, Go
``interface{}``, jq and int64 stores such as SQLite lose such a value as a
JSON number with no error. Quantities, such as sizes, counts, offsets,
ticks and IDs, are JSON numbers.

A key is absent when Speakeasy did not collect its data: its option is off,
or the data does not apply, such as the memory layout in kernel mode. An
empty list or object means that Speakeasy collected the data and found
nothing. A counter or a boolean is always present when Speakeasy collects
it, also when it is 0 or false.

emulation_total_runtime.description: Wall-clock time in seconds, rounded to milliseconds, from the first start of the run queue to the end of the emulation.
emulation_total_runtime.title: Emulation Total Runtime

timestamp.description: Unix time in seconds of the first start of the run queue.
timestamp.title: Timestamp

path.description: Host path of the input file. Absent when the input came from bytes.
path.title: Path

size.description: Size of the input in bytes.
size.title: Size

image_base.description: Base address of the input image in the emulator. Rebase a disassembler database to this address to match the addresses of the report.
image_base.title: Image Base

errors.description: Errors that do not belong to one run, such as an ``invalid_image`` defect of the input PE.
errors.title: Errors

strings.description: Strings of the input and of memory. Only with ``memory.strings``.

data.description: Payloads of the report, keyed by SHA-256. Each ``data_ref`` field holds a key of this mapping.
data.title: Data

processes.description: Processes of the runs and of the events, in the order of ``pid``. A kernel-mode run has no process, so in kernel mode the list has only the targets of process and memory events.
processes.title: Processes

runs.description: Runs of the emulation, in the order that the runs started.
runs.title: Runs

title: Report
